unit.why: A biographical frame about R. Alexander (Sender) the shohet, the Besht's scribe, holds two separate narratives: the Besht's account of his ascent to the Garden of Eden, and how Sender's fingernails grew deformed after he exorcised a spirit for the Besht.

stories.start_quote: עוד מעניני התגלות הבעש״ט ראשית דבר
stories.end_quote: וגם אותך סענדירל ראיתי בתוכם ונשארת אונטר שטעלינג
stories.summary_en: The narrator's father-in-law, R. Alexander, was the Besht's scribe for eight years and later a shohet. R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne used to remind him at the third Sabbath meal of the Besht's ascent to the Garden of Eden: there only a few people stayed with the Besht up to the Tree of Life, Sender among them, though he remained on a lower rung.

stories.start_quote: וגם לא היה לו על יד ימין
stories.summary_en: The Besht sent Sender to adjure a madman. At night the spirit frightened Sender, so he visualized holy names on his hand and struck the spirit, bleeding from under his nails. From then on his nails grew abnormally, and the Besht came at once to calm his fear.
